$comment: Sensitivity map for EVERY path in the kit. Consumed by the equip skill (payload filtering) and by kit-guard (CI enforcement). Folder position is never the boundary — this file is. Add a path => add its marker in the same commit; unmatched paths are treated as norfolk-only (fail closed). Addresses SpecFlow finding C4.

$sensitivities.client-safe: May be copied into any repo, any org.
$sensitivities.norfolk-only: May be copied into Norfolk-Group repos only.
$sensitivities.client:<id>: May be copied into that client's repos only.
$sensitivities.kit-only: NEVER copied anywhere. Lives in the kit and is READ by the Manual app, not distributed. No org allows it, so the existing filter handles it with no extra machinery — this is the kit's own working material (its plans, its decision records, its Owner's Guide), and copying it into a repo would fork the kit, which is the exact failure the Manual exists to prevent.

$kitLocal.$comment: The kit's OWN working material. Never shipped, and — critically — NOT listed in `markers` below. Anything in `markers` is a path the guard polices in every equipped repo, so listing `README.md` or `docs/plans/**` there would forbid every repo from having its own README or its own plans. These paths are kit-local instead: equip never ships them (they fall to unmatchedDefault = kit-only), and the guard ignores identically-named files in target repos because those belong to the repo, not the kit. The Manual app reads these from the kit at render time. Found 2026-07-31, when the first equipped repo could not have been given a README.

$excludeFromPayload.$comment: Paths with a legitimate sensitivity that equip nevertheless does NOT ship, for reasons unrelated to sensitivity. Kept separate from `markers` on purpose: a marker answers 'who may hold this', an exclusion answers 'is this worth shipping'. kit-guard still enforces the marker if one of these ever turns up in a repo, so an exclusion is never a security control — only a payload decision.
$excludeFromPayload.brand/**: 180MB, overwhelmingly Illustrator masters and social banners. Shipping it would put 180MB in every repo. Curated web sets (SVG/PNG at web sizes) are a Phase 4 task; until they exist, no brand ships anywhere. Sensitivity markers below stay accurate so the guard keeps working.
$excludeFromPayload.src/**: 46 files of animation components: 19 specimens plus _replit-export/, the Replit-authored variants — kept deliberately, Ricardo rates them. Excluded from the DEFAULT payload only: most repos need no animation library, and installing one nobody asked for is the kitchen-sink antipattern. A repo that wants them asks by name. (Ricardo, 2026-07-31: 'do not stuff too much graphics and junk in the repo.')

$unmatchedDefaultRationale: kit-only, not norfolk-only. `norfolk-only` LOOKS fail-closed but is not: Norfolk-Group allows that sensitivity, so an unmarked file ships silently into every Norfolk repo. Found on 2026-07-31 when `git ls-files` quoted a path containing an accent (OBRA PÍA), the quoted form matched no pattern, and a KIT Capital client asset was about to be copied into a Norfolk repo. `kit-only` is allowed by no org, so an unmarked file ships nowhere and someone notices the absence.
